outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit admission rate
cohort: 109,722 women with singleton pregnancies who delivered after 28 weeks of gestation at thirty-nine hospitals in mainland China in 2011
finding: Male fetuses were associated with a higher incidence of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm birth, macrosomia, caesarean delivery, and neonatal complications, compared to female fetuses in a Chinese population.
mod_finding: Male fetuses were associated with an increased incidence of operative vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery, and cephalopelvic disproportion/failure to progress.
